description.narrative:
PUI is a front line humanitarian actor operating in hard to reach areas with a particular focus on health in emergencies. PUI operates in 24 countries and the majority of these face extreme and very high access constraints. According to The Assessment Capacities Project (ACAPS) ranking (July 2023) PUI is operating in 6 out of 7 humanitarian crises with extreme access constraints and 9 out of 11 crises with very high access constraints. The majority (around 40%) of PUI’s budget is directed towards health interventions. PUI also works in areas of nutrition, food security and livelihoods (FSL) together with economic recovery, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), protection and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). PUI implements roughly around 210 projects per year. PUI's support reaches around six million people per year.
Sida entered into an agreement with PUI in 2023 on the basis that they were considered to add value to Sida’s humanitarian portfolio and contribute to the goals in the Humanitarian Strategy (2021¬2025) in terms of providing health services and integrating nutrition interventions to affected communities in hard to reach areas

PUI är en humanitär organisation som arbetar i svårtillgängliga områden i humanitära kriser, ofta i frontlinjen, och har ett särskilt fokus på hälsa. PUI är verksamma i 24 länder och majoriteten av dessa humanitära kriser har extrema eller mycket höga tillträdesbegränsningar. Enligt en rankning från The Assessment Capacities Project (ACAPS) verkar PUI i sex av sju humanitära kriser med extrema tillträdesbegränsningar och i nio av elva kriser med mycket höga tillträdesbegränsningar. Omkring 40% av PUI:s verksamhet är inriktad på hälsa. PUI arbetar också inom områdena nutrition, tryggad livsmedelsförsörjning och uppehälle, vatten, sanitet och hygien, skydd samt psykisk hälsa och psykosocialt stöd. PUI genomför ungefär 210 projekt per år. Organisationen når cirka sex miljoner människor per år.
Sida ingick avtal med PUI 2023 utifrån att de ansågs ge ett mervärde till Sidas humanitära portfölj och bidra till målen i den humanitära strategin (2021­-2025) när det gäller att tillhandahålla hälsotjänster och integrera nutritionsinsatser till drabbade människor i svårtillgängliga humanitära kriser.

This contribution aims to support PUI in selected humanitarian crisis where PUI will implement specific projects and where the organisation has a clear added value to provide humanitarian assistance and protection to crisis affected populations. Sida will support PUI's humanitarian interventions in three different crises in 2023.
Sudan (10 MSEK) - PUI proposes a project cantered on providing health and nutrition assistance. The intervention's target area is a destination for many displaced people living in IDP camps and suffering from severe health issues and malnutrition. GBV has been identified as a targeted area in which PUI will provide direct support through health centres as well as community awareness raising. Sida considers PUI to be an important partner in Sudan. The organisation's programmatic focus responds well to the Sudan Humanitarian Response Plan's (HRP) priority humanitarian needs. Sida provides support to PUI with a focus on health and nutrition to Al Geneina and Kereneik in West Darfur. Through PUI's program, existing health system will be supported by providing basic health and nutrition services integrated with psychosocial support (PSS) to vulnerable population groups.
Objective: Support the existing health system with provision of essential health and nutrition services integrated with PSS to vulnerable populations in West Darfur, Sudan.
Colombia (7 MSEK) - PUI have proposed a 12-month project together with Fundación Halü built upon their current experience to support access and protection of sexual and reproductive health rights of the most vulnerable population, particularly Venezuelan settled migrants and crisis-affected Colombians. The action will focus on Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW), women, children and adolescents in rural and peri-urban communities surrounding Tame, Arauquita and Saravena (Arauca) and Tibú (Norte de Santander). PUI will provide direct access to sexual and reproductive health (SRH), Mental Health and psychosocial care to the crisis-affected population in Arauca and Tibú, with a focus on recognition and response to the specific risks and vulnerabilities of women and girls, while Fundación Halü, will improve access to mechanisms of prevention and response to SGBV and child violence in Tibú (Norte de Santander) municipality. The partners will seek complementarity and synergy through an integrated intervention based on a community approach in order to strengthen the projects impact.
Objective: Increased immediate access to health/mental health services and protection response to target population.
Central African Republic (8 MSEK) - PUI proposes a health, nutrition and WASH project that will cover the needs of 27,448 individuals, including 6,681 direct beneficiaries through targeted free care (including 1,098 pregnant women, 834 lactating women and 4,749 children from 0 to 59 months) and 20,767 indirect beneficiaries through the improvement of healthcare provision in the 3 health facilities (Djamassinda, Zoukoutouniala and Bangbali) and the health district hospital of Bamingui-Bangoran Prefecture in Ndélé. These health facilities have been targeted in consultation with the local Health District.
Objective: Ensure access to quality primary healthcare and to malnutrition treatments for the crisis-affected populations.

description.narrative:
This is a summary of the results from PUI's activity year April 2024 - March 2025 as the reporting for the activity year April 2025 - March 2026 will be shared with Sida September 2026. The Conclusion of Performance published May 2026 does not cover the results for April 2025 - March 2026 for the same reason but results from this period will be covered by the Completion Memo.
The focal point for PUI at Sida takes note that PUI managed to support a total of 202,237 direct beneficiaries in the sectors of health, water and sanitation (WASH), psychosocial support, nutrition and sexual and reproductive health and rights with 50,527,895 SEK in 2024. This is an overall overachievement of 54 % compared to the initially target of 131,372 direct beneficiaries.
Sida recall that PUI's project in Colombia enabled support to 10,905 direct beneficiaries in Catatumbo and Arauca in between April 2024 and March 2025. PUIs project in Colombia focused on vulnerable communities, where it concentrates on providing basic healthcare services, promoting sexual and reproductive health, and offering psychosocial support to vulnerable populations. The project budget was 8 MSEK and PUIs project were able to reach 10,905 people instead of the planned 8,730 an overachievement with 25 % of beneficiaries initially targeted. PUI together with partner Halü, channeling Sida funding, reached 6,216 direct beneficiaries (an overachievement of 38 % compared to the beneficiaries targeted) within the health sector, 5,273 beneficiaries (an overachievement of 25 % compared to the beneficiaries initially targeted) within the protection sector. The overachievement can in part be explained by learning from previous engagement in the region as well as an unexpected interest in protection and psychosocial support by educational institutions.
Sida recall that PUI's project in Sudan enabled support to 16,320 direct beneficiaries in El Geneina locality, West Darfur in between April 2024 and April 2025. A challenging operational environment due to conflict, flooding and severe and changing humanitarian conditions of the population resulted in PUI decreasing the initial targeted of 31,552 beneficiaries to 12,650 beneficiaries in its first modification request approved by Sida on the 18th of September. PUI managed to exceed its modified number of targeted beneficiaries with 29 %. PUI's project contributed to the improvement of the health and nutrition of crises affected populations in West Darfur and Central Darfur in Sudan, providing life saving health and nutrition services integrated with psychosocial support. The project budget was 12 MSEK which was fully utilized during the project. Sida was continuously informed of the challenges met by PUI during the project and therefor the result is motivated and comprehensible given severe humanitarian context and unpredictable context with need for sudden reprioritization. After the approval of a modification request Sida funding was also utilized to cover gap in funding after the USAID freeze and closure of funds for one of PUI's projects. In order to optimize the number of people reached with Sida funding and make sure the implementation of a phaseout and exit strategy a no-cost extension was approved for additional one month for the project. In total PUI reached 14,335 direct beneficiaries within the health sector (an overachievement of 30 % compared to the beneficiaries targeted after the first modification request), 1,353 direct beneficiaries within the nutrition sector (an overachievement of 85 % compared to the beneficiaries targeted after the first modification request) and 632 direct beneficiaries in the sector of psychosocial health (an under achievement of 30 % compared to the beneficiaries targeted after the first modification request). The underachievement was due to the delay in start of the project due to the change in the selection of health facility supported as well as lower community participation in psychosocial support activities than anticipated in the beginning of the project.
Sida recall that PUI's project in CAR enabled support to 44,182 beneficiaries in Bamingui Bangoran prefectures in between 1st of April 2024 30th of March 2025. PUI implemented a project for an integrated Health and Nutrition response including WASH in Health and WASH in Nutrition with integrated psychosocial support for populations affected by the humanitarian crisis in the health centers of Bangbali, Djamassinda, Kotissako (new in 2024), Zoukoutouniala, the health posts of Ngarba and Boulkinia and the district hospital of Ndélé. The project budget was 10 MSEK and PUIs project were able to reach 44,182 people instead of the planned 13,275, an overachievement with 233 % of beneficiaries initially targeted. In the sector of health this was an over achievement of 23 % and in the sector of nutrition this was an overachievement of 140 %. The overachievements can be explained by the push factor of free care to seek health and nutrition services as well as UNICEF supply of nutrition inputs to PUI led services. Nevertheless an underachievement of 78 % was noted on the activity of medical care to GBV survivors and referral to psychosocial support due to challenges to have beneficiaries seeking help due to the sensitive nature of the support. Challenges in the implementation were communicated continuously with Sida during the project but does not seem to have affected results achievements much as many challenges were managed promptly. Close to the end of the project in CAR PUI requested to utilize underspending due to low implementation rate of psychosocial support activities to cover costs in the project in order to keep fundamental functions in the project ongoing that would otherwise have to be terminated due to cut in funds by other donors. Sida approved parts of the modification request using underspending for those budget lines that contributed to the direct aid delivery. PUI reimbursed Sida for the remaining of the underspending in 29th of October 2025 on a total of 472,105 SEK. This modification made possible the full implementation of the project and the overall overachievement of 233 %.
Sida recall that PUI's project in the DRC enabled support to 52,623 direct beneficiaries in the provinces of North Kivu and Ituri in between 1st of April 2024 and 30th of April 2026. PUI implemented an integrated health, nutrition, protection and psychosocial support project through the deployment of mobile clinics in order to respond to the protracted and massive population displacements in the provinces close to active conflict in this hard-to-reach areas where few to no other health actors have presence. The project budget was 15 MSEK and after communication with PUI on the narrative report 2024 it was clarified that PUI was able to reach 52,623 direct beneficiaries instead of the initially targeted 35,868 an overachievement of 47 %, an overachievement of 12 % in the sectors of health and nutrition together and an overachievement of 300 % in the sector of protection. Overachievements in protection was explained by the higher than expected number of awareness-raising sessions. High results in nutrition and health was explained by the high and during the implementation period increasing humanitarian needs due to the increasing conflict in the area. PUI communicated about challenges and changes during the project continuously during the project and PUI was able to swiftly adapt their project after the M23 takeover of Goma due to their mobile approach. Sida approved of a no-cost extension of one month in order for the emergency intervention following the worsening of humanitarian conditions after the M23 takeover.
In 2024 PUI received 6 MSEK for projects subject to the Sida RRM. PUI utilized all the funds for six different projects in Nigeria, Ethiopia, Burkina Faso, Ukraine, Colombia and Palestine within the sectors of nutrition, Health, Food Security and WASH. In total these funds made possible emergent support to 78,207 direct beneficiaries and overachievement of 29 % compared to the 60,849 initially targeted taking in all projects together. Each RRM project had an overachievement in between 13 and 48 %. Challenges in the projects and needs for revision of initial budgets and project plans were communicated to Sida throughout the projects. In the RRM for Ethiopia PUI requested a modification of the project close to the end of the project based on an underspending of funds due to a de facto exchange gain that they requested to be utilized for addressing acute needs within prevention of the spread of cholera in the original implementation area. Considering results for beneficiaries targeted by the RRM had already been reached as well as the urgency in the needs considered Sida approved of the modification request and made a decision on amendment of the contribution. The modification resulted in PUI training additionally 35 members of a Cholera Rapid Response Team and 70 community volunteers, including community and local leaders, in cholera surveillance and prevention. Additionally, food was provided to patients and caregivers admitted to Cholera Treatment Units, and hygiene materials were distributed to 120 displaced households in Kutir Hulet and China Camp.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
